event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: COVID-19 is treated by EOG as a recent, still-evolving threat that has already produced concrete, material harm and could trigger further operational, financial and supply-chain distress.  The 2022 filing date sits less than two years after the steep pandemic-induced commodity collapse of 1H-2020, so the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  EOG’s language moves along a continuum: (i) generic acknowledgements that pandemics influence prices, (ii) company-specific narratives of the 2020 cash-flow hit and share-price damage, and (iii) forward-looking warnings about renewed price shocks, counter-party defaults, labour shortages, remote-work costs and supply-chain disruptions.  These disclosures are largely aggravating (few mitigants other than a brief note that prices have ‘recovered’).  Because the statements identify both realised and potential impacts on cash flow, capital spending, workforce availability and supply logistics—and because the event is recent—overall risk is assessed as elevated.  Individual snippet scores therefore cluster in the upper mid-range (4-9), with variation driven by specificity, direct linkage to COVID-19, presence of quantified or ‘materially adverse’ language, and whether the impact is historical (higher weight) or merely hypothetical (lower weight).

components.reason: Explicitly names the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic as a factor that can disrupt prices and finances.
Statement is generic and embedded in a longer bullet list – limited company-specific detail.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides a direct but generic linkage; raises risk modestly without supplying company-specific impact.

evidence_list.snippet: Global or national health concerns, including a widespread outbreak of contagious disease, can, among other impacts, negatively impact the global economy, reduce demand and pricing for crude oil, NGLs and natural gas, lead to operational disruptions and limit our ability to execute on our business plan, any of which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Details multiple impact channels—demand destruction, price reduction, operational disruption.
Uses strong wording ‘materially and adversely affect’ company performance.
Prospective (could) rather than realised impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive description of potential material harm across markets and operations merits high score.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, the current pandemic involving a highly transmissible and pathogenic coronavirus (COVID-19) and the measures being taken to address and limit the spread of the virus have adversely affected the economies and financial markets of the world, resulting in an economic downturn that negatively impacted global demand and prices for crude oil, NGLs and natural gas.

components.reason: Directly links present COVID-19 pandemic to adverse macroeconomic effects.
Specifies negative impact on demand and commodity prices, key revenue drivers.
Event is ongoing and recent, increasing severity under Time Decay Principle.
Focuses on sector-wide rather than company-specific data.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recent, direct causal language and clear revenue linkage push score into upper range.

evidence_list.snippet: In fact, the substantial declines in crude oil, NGLs and natural gas prices that occurred in the first half of 2020 as a result of the economic downturn and overall reduction of demand prompted by the COVID-19 pandemic (and the oversupply of crude oil from certain foreign oil-exporting countries) materially and adversely affected the amount of cash flows we had available for our 2020 capital expenditures and other operating expenses, our results of operations during the first half of 2020 and the trading price of our common stock.

components.reason: Cites realised, historical impact directly attributable to COVID-19.
Specifies financial metrics harmed—cash flows, cap-ex, operating expenses.
Mentions impact on trading price, reflecting investor risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highest-severity evidence: concrete past damage, multiple financial dimensions, recent timeframe.

evidence_list.snippet: While the prices for crude oil, NGLs and natural gas have since recovered to at or above pre-pandemic levels, if such price declines were to reoccur and continue for an extended period of time, our cash flows and results of operations would be further adversely affected, as could the trading price of our common stock.

components.reason: Flags future downside risk to cash flow, operations and share price.
Explicit conditional language (‘if’) signals possibility not certainty.
States that prices have recovered—partial mitigation.
Links risk to repeated pandemic-type price shocks.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking risk balanced by note of current recovery; severity mid-low.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, if the COVID-19 outbreak should worsen, we may also experience disruptions to commodities markets, equipment supply chains and the availability of our workforce, which could materially and adversely affect our ability to conduct our business and operations.

components.reason: Identifies specific operational vulnerabilities: supply chain and labour.
Uses ‘materially and adversely affect’ regarding core operations.
Contingent wording (‘if’)—risk not yet realised.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Granular description of potential supply-chain and workforce disruptions yields high risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, if the COVID-19 outbreak were to worsen, resulting in another economic downturn, our customers and other contractual parties may be unable to pay amounts owed to us from time to time and to otherwise satisfy their contractual obligations to us, and may be unable to access the credit and capital markets for such purposes.

components.reason: Highlights counterparty credit risk linked to pandemic-driven downturn.
Specifies inability to pay obligations—direct cash-flow threat.
Conditional future scenario (‘may’) lessens current severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Credit-risk channel is material though still hypothetical, producing solid mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: Such inability of our customers and other contractual counterparties may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

components.reason: States direct material adverse effect on multiple financial metrics.
Dependent on prior conditional statement—no new causal detail.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds emphatic language but limited incremental information; moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: There are still too many variables and uncertainties regarding the COVID-19 pandemic, including the duration and severity of the outbreak; the emergence, contagiousness and threat of new and different strains of the virus; the development, availability, acceptance, and effectiveness of treatments or vaccines; the extent of travel restrictions, business closures and other measures imposed by governmental authorities; disruptions in the supply chain; a prolonged delay in the resumption of operations by one or more contractual parties; an increasingly competitive labor market due to a sustained labor shortage or increased turnover caused by the COVID-19 pandemic; increased logistics costs; additional operating costs due to remote working arrangements, adherence to social distancing guidelines, and other COVID-19-related challenges; increased risk of cyberattacks on information technology systems used in remote working arrangements; increased privacy-related risks due to processing health-related personal information; absence of employees due to illness; the impact of the pandemic on EOG's customers and contractual counterparties; and other factors that are currently unknown or considered immaterial, to fully assess the potential impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple operational and financial risk vectors (supply chain, labour, logistics, cybersecurity).
Acknowledges uncertainty and inability to fully assess impact—signals high unknown risk.
All risks are forward-looking but credible within ongoing pandemic timeframe.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed catalogue of specific pandemic-driven uncertainties justifies strong score.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of the many uncertainties associated with ... (ii) the COVID-19 pandemic and its continuing effect on the economies and financial markets of the world ... EOG is unable to predict what changes may occur in crude oil and condensate, NGLs and natural gas prices in the future.

components.reason: Links pandemic uncertainty to inability to forecast commodity prices—a key revenue driver.
Highlights ongoing nature (‘continuing effect’).
Does not quantify or give direct company impact beyond forecasting limitation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows forecasting risk but lacks depth on financial consequences, yielding moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic and the measures taken to address and limit the spread of the virus adversely affected the economies and financial markets of the world, resulting in an economic downturn beginning in early 2020 that negatively impacted global demand and prices for crude oil and condensate, NGLs and natural gas.

components.reason: Retrospective statement: confirms actual adverse impact on demand and prices.
Directly attributes effect to COVID-19 pandemic.
Focuses on sector-wide rather than company-specific impact, but still revenue-critical.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Historical evidence of pandemic-triggered price collapse—material but less granular than cash-flow sentence.
